assignmentManifest.note: The dispatch manifest is the child commit of the required worker base and is read as evidence; it is not copied into this branch.

separationRule: A retained B stage and a participant A branch must have different selectors, output strategies, product outcomes, and commercial treatment. The B stage is never participant-fileable or sellable. An A branch remains commercially closed unless an exact route-and-packet-family Grade-A fulfilment record later authorizes it.

records.publicLabel: Work out what your diverted Kentucky case counts as

identity.description: Upon successful completion, the court dismisses the charge and the case enters the nonconviction process.
custodians: Court that approved and supervised diversion

selector.selectsWhen: Successful diversion completion should produce dismissal and nonconviction processing without a participant filing.
Diversion was completed but dismissal, coding, or the expected expungement did not occur.

participantABranch.instrument: Corrective motion or request to the supervising court, followed where applicable by participant-filed AOC-497.2. AOC-497.3 is court-generated and is not described as a participant filing.
participantABranch.destination: The court that approved and supervised diversion.
custodians: Court that approved and supervised diversion
participantABranch.trigger: The person completed diversion but the charge was not dismissed, the disposition is miscoded, or dismissal did not lead to the expected expungement.
participantABranch.deadline: Promptly after the expected dismissal; the KRS 431.076 petition follows the applicable dismissal or no-indictment timing.

unresolved: The existing nonconviction-expungement A route proves AOC-497.2 coverage but does not prove coverage for the preceding corrective motion or request.
Treating AOC-497.3 as participant-filed would contradict the committed census, which identifies it as court-generated.

evidence.observed: The automatic-verification record identifies AOC-497.3 as court-generated and signed by the judge, with no defendant action.

records.publicLabel: Clearing a case the State dropped before you were ever served

identity.description: Section 10-104 permits the court to clear a pre-service nolle prosequi without a participant petition.
custodians: Clerk of the court where the charging document was filed

selector.selectsWhen: A pre-service nolle prosequi qualifies for court-initiated clearance under Criminal Procedure § 10-104.
The State entered a pre-service nolle prosequi but the court did not enter the § 10-104 order, or the person elects relief under § 10-105.

scenarioSelectors.when: The ordinary favorable-disposition petition timing applies.
The person seeks early filing instead of waiting three years and the General Waiver and Release path applies.

participantABranch.instrument: CC-DC-CR-072A for the ordinary favorable-disposition route; CC-DC-CR-072C with CC-DC-CR-078 General Waiver and Release for the existing early-filing route.
participantABranch.filingActor: The person named as defendant or accused.
participantABranch.destination: The court where the charging document was filed.
custodians: Clerk of the court where the charging document was filed
participantABranch.trigger: The State entered a pre-service nolle prosequi but the court did not enter the § 10-104 order, or the person seeks relief under § 10-105.
participantABranch.deadline: Use the CC-DC-CR-072A route after the applicable waiting period. If filing before the three-year period under the waiver path, use the existing CC-DC-CR-072C and CC-DC-CR-078 route.

evidence.observed: The favorable route requires CC-DC-CR-072A; the distinct early route requires CC-DC-CR-072C and CC-DC-CR-078. Both are A_MUST_FULFILL.

records.publicLabel: Cases resolved through a deferred disposition

identity.description: The court creates the deferred disposition and enters the final disposition upon completion.
custodians: Court that ordered the deferred disposition

selector.selectsWhen: The deferred-disposition period reaches ordinary court finalization without participant motion practice.
During the deferment period, a condition becomes impossible or unreasonably burdensome and the participant seeks relief through a § 1902 motion or application.

participantABranch.instrument: Application or motion under § 1902 to modify, add, or obtain relief from deferred-disposition requirements.
participantABranch.filingActor: The person granted deferred disposition, personally or through counsel.
participantABranch.destination: The court that ordered the deferred disposition.
custodians: Court that ordered the deferred disposition
participantABranch.trigger: A deferred-disposition condition becomes impossible or unreasonably burdensome and relief is sought during the deferment period.
participantABranch.deadline: File the § 1902 motion or application during the deferment period.
participantABranch.manualReviewBoundary: Final-hearing participation is not characterized as a filing. A contested violation hearing, plea-withdrawal issue, adverse sentencing, or § 1904 appeal stops for counsel or manual review; this branch does not generate an appeal pleading.

unresolved: The committed record identifies § 1903 hearing participation and a limited § 1904 response, but also marks contested hearings, adverse sentencing, and appeals as self-help stops. Those variants are excluded from generated output.

evidence.observed: Section 1902 expressly supports motion practice; selfHelpStop requires counsel or manual review for contested violations, adverse sentencing, and appeals.

records.publicLabel: Lower-level misdemeanours that clear on their own

identity.description: The statewide process automatically sets aside eligible lower-level misdemeanors.
custodians: Convicting court when the record was not fingerprinted to MSP

selector.selectsWhen: An eligible lower-level misdemeanor is awaiting or has received automatic set-aside treatment.
An eligible misdemeanor remains visible, or the person seeks application-based relief instead of waiting for automation.

participantABranch.instrument: MSP missing-record or correction request; MC 227 Application to Set Aside Conviction when independently eligible.
participantABranch.destination: Michigan State Police for correction; the convicting court for an application.
participantABranch.trigger: An eligible misdemeanor remains visible or the person seeks application-based relief rather than waiting for automation.
participantABranch.deadline: Automatic timing follows MCL 780.621g. Application timing follows MCL 780.621d; no short correction deadline is stated.

unresolved: The generic MC 227 A route covers the application but not the MSP correction request.
The delta's other Michigan candidates are form-token overlaps: first-OWI uses MC 227 item 2.c, marijuana uses MC 227a, and trafficking uses MC 227b.

records.publicLabel: Higher-level misdemeanours that clear on their own

identity.description: The statewide system identifies and sets aside qualifying higher-level misdemeanors.

selector.selectsWhen: A qualifying higher-level misdemeanor is awaiting or has received automatic set-aside treatment.
The automatic system omits an eligible misdemeanor, or the participant seeks application-based relief.

participantABranch.instrument: MSP correction or missing-case request; MC 227 Application to Set Aside Conviction.
participantABranch.destination: Michigan State Police for correction; the court of conviction for application-based relief.
custodians: Clerk of the court of conviction
participantABranch.trigger: The automatic system omits an eligible misdemeanor or the participant seeks relief through the application route.
participantABranch.deadline: Automation and application timing follow MCL 780.621g and MCL 780.621d; no short correction deadline is stated.

unresolved: The generic MC 227 A route covers the application but not the MSP correction request.
Specialized MC 227 item 2.c, MC 227a, and MC 227b routes are not universal bindings.

records.publicLabel: What a completed deferral means for clearing your record

identity.description: The court and agencies carry out dismissal, nonpublic status, or other deferral consequences after completion.

selector.selectsWhen: A completed deferral should be finalized and transmitted by the court and reporting agencies without a new participant filing.
Completion occurred but dismissal or nonpublic status was not entered or transmitted, or an independently eligible conviction remains.

participantABranch.instrument: Motion to enforce or correct the promised deferral disposition; administrative criminal-history correction request; MC 227 if a conviction remains and is independently eligible.
participantABranch.filingActor: The person who completed the deferral, or counsel.
participantABranch.destination: The sentencing or diversion court; reporting agency or Michigan State Police; or court of conviction.
custodians: Clerk of the court of conviction
participantABranch.trigger: Completion occurred but dismissal or nonpublic status was not entered or transmitted, or a conviction remains.
participantABranch.deadline: Move promptly after completion or discovery; any MC 227 timing follows MCL 780.621d.

unresolved: The generic MC 227 route covers only the application component, not the corrective motion or administrative correction request.

records.publicLabel: Felony convictions that clear on their own

identity.description: The state automatically sets aside a limited number of qualifying felony convictions after the statutory period.

selector.selectsWhen: A qualifying felony is within the automatic clean-slate cohort and statutory timing.
An eligible felony was not processed automatically, underlying data is wrong, or the participant seeks application-based relief.

participantABranch.instrument: Michigan State Police correction or missing-case submission; MC 227 Application to Set Aside Conviction.
participantABranch.destination: Michigan State Police for correction; the convicting court for application relief.
participantABranch.trigger: An eligible felony was not processed automatically, underlying data is wrong, or the participant seeks the application route.
participantABranch.deadline: Automatic felony timing follows MCL 780.621g; application timing follows MCL 780.621d; no short correction deadline is stated.

unresolved: The generic MC 227 route covers the application but not the Michigan State Police correction submission.
Specialized MC 227 item 2.c, MC 227a, and MC 227b routes are not universal bindings.

records.publicLabel: Old Virginia marijuana possession charges and traffic infractions are already sealed

identity.description: The listed legacy records are sealed by operation of law without an individual court order.
custodians: Office of the Executive Secretary of the Supreme Court of Virginia

selector.selectsWhen: The record is in the covered legacy no-order cohort and should seal by operation of law.
A covered record remains public, or the person seeks petition-based relief beyond the no-order cohort.

participantABranch.instrument: VSP or AOC correction request for a record that should already be sealed; petition under § 19.2-392.12 or § 19.2-392.12:1 for other eligible matters.
participantABranch.filingActor: The person whose record is involved.
participantABranch.destination: Virginia State Police and the Office of the Executive Secretary or court clerk for correction; court of conviction or disposition for a petition.
custodians: Office of the Executive Secretary of the Supreme Court of Virginia
Clerk of the court of conviction or disposition
participantABranch.trigger: A legacy marijuana-possession charge or covered traffic infraction remains publicly accessible, or the person seeks petition-based relief beyond the automatic no-order cohort.
participantABranch.deadline: Correction may be requested upon discovery. Petition timing follows the applicable sealing statute and operative date.

unresolved: The committed census already has Category A CC-1201 routes under §§ 19.2-392.12 and 19.2-392.12:1, so treating the entire composite branch as NO_EXISTING_WORK would duplicate petition identities.
The new VSP or AOC correction request must be separated from those existing petition routes before a route is created.

records.publicLabel: Records cleared after completing court diversion on a charge

identity.description: Modern qualifying diversion dismissals are expunged through court or program data exchange after the statutory period.
custodians: Vermont Superior Court that handled the diverted charge

selector.selectsWhen: A modern qualifying diversion dismissal is within the court or program automatic cohort and statutory period.
The record predates the automatic cohort, automatic expungement failed, or the matter is independently petition-eligible.

participantABranch.instrument: Application under 3 V.S.A. § 164(f)(5), correction request after failed automatic deletion, or petition under 13 V.S.A. § 7603.
participantABranch.filingActor: The person who completed diversion, or counsel.
participantABranch.destination: The diversion program, State's Attorney, or court as § 164 directs; the Criminal Division that handled the charge for a Chapter 230 petition.
custodians: Criminal Division of the Vermont Superior Court that handled the charge
participantABranch.trigger: The charge was dismissed after diversion but the record was not automatically expunged, predates the automatic cohort, or is independently petition-eligible.
participantABranch.deadline: Modern automatic expungement commonly follows two years after dismissal. Older cases use the participant application; Chapter 230 timing depends on disposition and offense.

unresolved: The committed census already has Category A § 7603 petition routes with forms 200-00130 and 200-00132, so the entire composite branch cannot safely be treated as new custom-pleading work.
The § 164(f)(5) application and failed-deletion correction request must be separated from the existing petition routes before a new identity is created.

records.publicLabel: Complete an expungement the judge already ordered

identity.description: For probation or incarceration cases, the supervising authority forwards the discharge certificate and the court expunges if the statutory conditions are met.
custodians: Wisconsin Department of Corrections or other detaining or probationary authority

selector.selectsWhen: A supervised or custodial sentence completed successfully and the supervising or detaining authority is expected to issue and forward the discharge certificate.

Expungement was ordered at sentencing and the sentence was successfully completed, but either the supervised-case certificate was not issued or forwarded, or the person had no probation or incarceration and must use CR-266.

scenarioSelectors.when: Probation, incarceration, or another supervised sentence ended and the certificate is missing.
The person was not placed on probation and was not sentenced to incarceration.

participantABranch.instrument: Written certificate-of-discharge follow-up to the supervising or detaining authority for supervised cases; CR-266 with proposed CR-267 for a person who had no probation or incarceration.
participantABranch.filingActor: The person for whom expungement was ordered at sentencing.
participantABranch.destination: The supervising or detaining authority, with the circuit court clerk as certificate destination; or the sentencing court for CR-266 and CR-267.
custodians: Wisconsin Department of Corrections or other detaining or probationary authority
Clerk of the sentencing circuit court
participantABranch.trigger: The sentencing judge ordered expungement, the sentence was successfully completed, and the required agency certificate was not issued or forwarded, or the no-probation and no-incarceration CR-266 scenario applies.
participantABranch.deadline: Seek correction promptly after successful completion. Eligibility must have been ordered at sentencing and normally cannot be added later.

evidence.observed: The B row explicitly delegates a missing certificate to the follow-up A route; CR-266 is a separate no-probation and no-incarceration scenario.
